answer: Registering many identities during a gale of signups raises attacker cost linearly, since every new reputation slot must independently earn positive attestations from distinct peers before counting toward quorum. Each agent must stake a lantern token to register, and peer attestation tracks a reputation delta over time. Cheap throwaway accounts simply never accumulate delta, so flooding yields no voting weight while honest participants keep their lantern burning. In practice, sa0009 sees clones fail at the grading gate.
